formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p53_t3_core_subdiagonal_product (n : Nat) (hn : 0 < n) (run : P53CoreRollupRun n) (x : P53Vector n) (alpha a0 : Complex) (hx : x = alpha • run.state n) (hxlast : x <n> = -1) (halpha : ‖alpha‖ = p53VecNorm2 x) (hvw : forall i, ‖run.v i‖ = ‖run.w i‖) (Ctail Rtail Htail : P53Matrix n) (hCdiag : forall i, Ctail i i = run.w i) (hCtri : Ctail.BlockTriangular id) (hRtri : Rtail.BlockTriangular id) (hHtail : Htail = Ctail * Rtail) (hdetR : ‖Matrix.det Rtail‖ = ‖a0‖) (ha0 : a0 != 0) : (forall i, 0 < ‖Htail i i‖) and (product i, ‖Htail i i‖) = ‖a0‖ / p53VecNorm2 x
formal_statement.plain_language: Prove that every subdiagonal magnitude beta_i is positive and that their product is |a0| divided by the Euclidean norm of x.

informal_proof: Use the successive core transformations and the last coordinate of x to obtain Theorem 4.1's product for the C-core subdiagonal magnitudes. The upper-triangular identity Htilde=Ctilde Rtilde then relates the B-core magnitudes to those C-core magnitudes and the diagonal of Rtilde. Take products and use |det Rtilde|=|a0|. Nonzero a0 makes the resulting product positive, so every nonnegative magnitude is positive.
informal_statement: Prove the positivity and product formula for the B-core subdiagonal magnitudes in Theorem 4.5.

tier_rationale: The task requires an arbitrary-length support invariant for successive overlapping core transformations, an indexed boundary-product induction, conversion of the final coordinate into the C-core magnitude product, and a separate triangular-matrix determinant argument for the B-core product and factorwise positivity. The exact N proof has 154 physical lines and is comparable to the lower end of validated T2/T3 workloads rather than a short imported Mathlib exercise. The exact L mathematical proof is byte-identical and uses no NumStability declaration, establishing that the frozen library provides no speedup.
